note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following diagnosis of high-grade prostate cancer.

The patient is an 82-year-old retired farmer who lives with his partner. He has a medical history of hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, coronary artery disease, and osteoarthritis. He takes valsartan, lisinopril, metoprolol, rosuvastatin, and paracetamol PRN. He is an ex-smoker (12 pack-yr, quit 2006) and drinks 12 units of alcohol per week. He plays tennis twice a week and reports moderate LUTS with an IPSS score of 9/35. He recently attended the pain clinic for chronic shoulder pain and the endocrine clinic for thyroid screening. His PSA has fluctuated significantly, rising from 5.0 ng/mL in Aug 2023 to 12.9 ng/mL in Feb 2024, dropping to 2.6 ng/mL in Aug 2024, and rising again to 14.0 ng/mL in Jan 2025.

Per rectum, the prostate feels smooth and symmetric without palpable nodules, consistent with a cT1c stage. The general examination is unremarkable, with stable vital signs and no signs of lymphadenopathy or bone tenderness.
